title: Adhesive, temperature-tolerant and dual-network self-powered n-type thermoelectric ionogel sensor for motion detection, information transmission and diabetes foot monitoring

segments.text: Flexible wearable sensors are widely used in health monitoring and motion tracking, but their limited environmental adaptability and dependence on external power sources restrict applications in complex scenarios and chronic disease management.
In this work, an n-type self-powered thermoelectric ionogel (iTE gel) was fabricated using ionic liquids with two-step approach under ultraviolet light crosslinking reaction.

The ionogel comprised a crosslinked network based on poly(poly(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate) (pPEGMA), a secondary network formed by polyionic liquids, and a composite of lithium salts and ionic liquids, achieving good stretchability (517%), mechanical strength (245.5 kPa), and a significant Seebeck effect (Se,-5.34 mV/K) while maintaining stability from-10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with outstanding temperature-tolerance.
Temperature gradients drive directional ion migration, enabling direct thermal-to-electrical energy conversion and intrinsic self-powering capabilities.
Structural optimization permitted simultaneous detection of temperature, pressure, and strain.

When integrated into a wearable platform, the system effectively achieved information transmission, monitored plantar pressure, gait patterns, and local temperature in diabetic foot patients, showing high sensitivity and stability during daily use.
This research advanced flexible sensor development with enhanced environmental adaptability, self-powering functionality, and long-term wearability.
